title: Engineering & Technology Skeleton v1
description: Coverage skeleton for the engineering-and-technology continent (seventh continent, parallel round v1 branch 13c, merge order 3): field/subfield two-level node set under domain:engineering-and-technology — civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, materials, environmental, aerospace, industrial and biotechnology-side engineering areas — each tagged with academic_status. Construction input only — not canonical graph data; nodes only, zero edges (skeleton-first). The junction node already canonical in /data (domain:engineering-and-technology, Q11023) is out of generation scope. Architecture is owned by round branch 13d (arts-and-design); life-science areas by 13b; biotechnology (FORD 2.8/2.9) is owned by this branch per the round boundary assignment table.

include: Engineering and technology field and subfield coverage skeleton (nodes only)
Civil-engineering-family areas under LCC TA/TC/TD/TE/TF/TG/TH and UDC 624-628 plus 69, FORD 2.1/2.7
Mechanical and aerospace areas under LCC TJ/TL and UDC 621/629, FORD 2.3
Electrical, electronic, telecommunication, computer and nuclear engineering areas under LCC TK and UDC 621.3/654, FORD 2.2
Chemical engineering and process areas under LCC TP and UDC 66, FORD 2.4
Materials, metallurgy and mining areas under LCC TA401-492/TN and UDC 620/622/669, FORD 2.5
Biotechnology under UDC 60 and LCC TP248.13-248.65, FORD 2.8/2.9 (owned by this branch per the round assignment table); biomedical engineering under FORD 2.6 with the medicine boundary pre-registered
Manufacturing and industrial-engineering areas under LCC T55.4-60.8/TS and UDC 67/68, FORD 2.11
Wikidata QID resolution for identity and external_ids
exclude: Edges and relations (skeleton-first: dots before lines; part_of skeleton edges are a separate batch)
Re-proposing any existing /data node (domain:engineering-and-technology and all 195 other canonical nodes; reconcile to existing IDs instead)

Architecture and architectural engineering (LCC NA + TH845-895, UDC 72): owned by round branch 13d per the boundary assignment table — engineering-side evidence is recorded in this batch's reports only, never as nodes

Control engineering as a node: subfield:control-theory already exists (formal sciences) with a domain-direct engineering membership edge (LCC TJ212-225); new control-related evidence (UDC 681.5) feeds the re-target review, not a new node

Operations research / industrial-engineering overlap: subfield:operations-research already exists (formal sciences, LCC T57.6-57.97 evidence on its domain-direct membership edge); no duplicate node — membership/adjacency and the re-target review only

Existing CS-owned boundary nodes: subfield:computer-security, subfield:cryptography, subfield:software-engineering, subfield:quantum-computing (NS membership), subfield:computer-systems and the rest of the CS continent — computer engineering (LCC TK7885-7895) is in-scope as a new node with a pre-registered CS dual-membership question

Existing NS-owned boundary nodes: subfield:optics, subfield:acoustics, subfield:plasma-physics (LCC TA1501-1820 applied optics/photonics, TA365-367 acoustical engineering, TA2001-2040 plasma engineering are engineering-side evidence, recorded for cross-listing review — photonics as a possibly-distinct referent is pre-registered)
Life-sciences areas (13b territory) and medicine (UDC 61, LCC R): medical-physics precedent governs deferrals; FORD 2.6 medical/biomedical engineering is the one pre-registered case-by-case exception
Management, business administration and accountancy (UDC 657/658/659 sit inside UDC 65 but belong to the social-sciences continent; engineering management evidence is recorded, not generated)
Photography (LCC TR), handicrafts (LCC TT), home economics (LCC TX): arts/practical-knowledge territory — recorded as out-of-continent, never generated
Military engineering (UDC 623; LCC UG sits in class U): pre-registered as likely deliberate non-coverage — record, do not generate without passing the dual criterion
Agriculture and food-science institutional territory (FORD 4): food engineering is the one pre-registered boundary seed (LCC TP368-456 + UDC 664 are in-continent homes)

notes: Continent launched as branch 13c of parallel round v1 (round design ratified by the CPO 2026-06-11; section-12 snapshot pin = commit d816cb6; promotion merge order 3 with the succession rule).

Coverage baseline for generation/QC: LCC class T outline (loc.gov outline PDF, fetched 2026-06-11; T/TA/TC/TD/TE/TF/TG/TH/TJ/TK/TL/TN/TP/TS captured in full, plus id.loc.gov authority records for cutter-level checks at QC), UDC class 6 records (60 Biotechnology, 62 Engineering with full 620-629 children, 65 boundary documentation, 66 chemical technology, 669 metallurgy, 67/68 manufacturing industries, 69 building trade — udcsummary.info getrecord endpoint, fetched 2026-06-11; query-string URLs are SPN-incompatible, citations are by notation + caption), and OECD FORD section 2 (2.1-2.11; arrs.si mirror, fetched 2026-06-11, existing snapshot web/20260611023459). No discipline-specific scheme is ratified gate-level for this continent (IEEE/ASME taxonomies were not promoted; LCC/UDC gate + FORD cross-check, with MSC and the arXiv taxonomy as auxiliary cross-checks only).

docs/data-foundry.md section 12 (including its precedent log, at pin d816cb6) is a mandatory input to the generation order (promotion policy v1.3); section 13 governs any multi-membership question raised during QC.

Pre-registered structural questions for QC: (1) computer-engineering vs the CS continent — LCC TK7885-7895 is an in-continent home; a CS-side second membership is a section-13 dual-membership candidate (Q428691 is a known computer-engineering QID, previously rejected only as an anchor for subfield:computer-systems); (2) materials-science boundary with chemistry/physics — section-13 candidates to record, not resolve; (3) industrial engineering's classification presence is thin (LCC T55.4-60.8 is a range inside class T; UDC files production engineering at 658.5 inside the management class) — dual-criterion test required, and its creation triggers the operations-research re-target review; (4) control engineering must NOT become a node (existing subfield:control-theory, formal sciences); TJ212-225 and UDC 681.5 evidence feeds the re-target review of the existing domain-direct membership edges; (5) electronics (TK7800-8360) is expected to absorb into electrical-engineering (label/absorption rules) unless the dual criterion separates them; (6) biomedical engineering (FORD 2.6) — LCC R856 and UDC 615.47 are medicine-class homes but the dominant institutional home is engineering schools, so cross-continent rule 3 does not fire on one prong; boundary recorded in uncertainty; (7) photonics vs the existing NS subfield:optics — distinct-referent test (quantum-information-science precedent): TA1501-1820 'Applied optics. Photonics' plus UDC 681.7 vs the physics referent; (8) naval-architecture-and-marine-engineering is a combined-name seed (LCC VM sits in class V, TC1501-1800 ocean engineering is in-continent, UDC 629.5 watercraft engineering) — combined-vs-split shape and any component-anchor question follow the umbrella-test precedent; (9) geomatics/surveying (TA501-625) is case-by-case per the round assignment table — if kept, the parked geodesy engineering-side evidence (TU Delft civil-engineering housing, session #12) is linked in this batch's report as a section-13 candidate, with any write-in deferred to session #14; (10) energy engineering inherits the NS deliberate-non-coverage record for 'energy science' as a cross-continent candidate (TJ163/TJ807-830 + UDC 620.9 + 662.6); (11) nuclear engineering's UDC presence sits below summary granularity (621.039 not visible at getrecord level) — single-visible-gate-scheme question pre-registered; (12) food engineering (TP368-456 + UDC 664 in-continent homes vs agriculture/food-science institutional homes, FORD 4) and textile engineering (UDC 677 + LCC TS1300-1865) are borderline seeds expected to live or die by the dual criterion; (13) highway (TE), railroad (TF) and bridge (TG) engineering are expected to absorb into transportation/civil engineering; sanitary engineering folds into environmental engineering by the label rule; (14) metallurgy and materials-science may coexist as peers if both pass the dual criterion (peer-coexistence rule); (15) bioengineering (TA164) folds into the biotechnology/biomedical-engineering pair — no third node without a distinct referent.

Post-skeleton re-target triggers recorded in the session order: operations-research and control-theory currently hold domain-direct engineering membership edges (session #7; LCC T57.6-57.97 and TJ212-225) — once proper in-continent parents exist, the re-target review runs under the mathematics-education precedent; information-theory's ECE-side membership is a parked section-13 candidate (session #8) — engineering-scheme filings are collected when the electrical-engineering field lands, written only if the evidence gate passes.
/data remains the source of truth for accepted graph data.
